news.title: Arsenal face possible ban from FIFA competitions - 'We have the power to act'
news.lede: The Independent Football Regulator has warned Arsenal and other Premier League giants that they could be excluded from future editions of FIFA tournaments if they disrupt the English calendar. That includes the coveted Club World Cup, which takes place once every four years outside of the usual Premier League season. Scheduling conflicts could jeopardise the participation of clubs like the Gunners, Manchester United and Liverpool moving forward - despite Chelsea winning last summer's maiden instalment of a 32-team competition. Regulator chair David Kogan told a Digital, Culture, Media and Sport committee: "There are clearly signs taking place from other entities - and FIFA is the obvious one - where it's creating global club competitions that currently sit outside the normal season of the English game and are every four years.

news.title: Shafaq News..Short Stature World Cup: Iraq awarded draw against Argentina
news.lede: Argentina’s 3-1 win over Iraq at the World Cup for footballers of short stature in Morocco was changed to a 1-1 draw after Iraq challenged the eligibility of Argentina’s No. 20, Hussein Jalil, head of Iraq’s short stature committee, told Shafaq News on Wednesday. Jalil said the ruling barred the player from the rest of the tournament. The draw takes Iraq to four points following its earlier win over Jordan.

news.title: Dutch football association backed FIFA president Infantino before reversing its position
news.lede: The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) initially backed Gianni Infantino's bid to remain FIFA president, even though it later withdrew its support for him. Secretary-general Gijs de Jong disclosed that the KNVB had personally handed Infantino a letter endorsing his candidacy shortly before changing its position. "The letter had no legal value whatsoever. At that moment, it was a strategic decision in the interests of Dutch football," De Jong said.

When Spain secured a joint bid for the 2030 World Cup, many automatically assumed as a certainty that the final match would take place on home turf.

news.title: Spain thought it had the 2030 World Cup final, yet Morocco had other plans
news.lede: MADRID/RABAT: When Spain won a joint bid to host the 2030 World Cup, officials at the national football association took it as given that the final would be held on their soil. As former world champions – a feat since repeated – and the world’s second-most visited country, Spain had the sporting pedigree and tourism know-how to welcome large crowds, so it was widely assumed the final would come to them. Co-host Portugal was not interested, while Spanish officials thought that Morocco, as a late addition to the bid, surely would not agitate for the final. But in recent months Spain has begun to fear that the North African nation, an emerging football power, could snatch the game’s biggest showpiece from under its nose.

news.title: Fijian youngster sets World Cup record as he chases professional dream
news.lede: Fijian teenager Ryan Nakul Swami has made football history by representing his country at two FIFA youth World Cups within three weeks. The forward is one of two players to achieve the feat, progressing from the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival in Azerbaijan to the FIFA U-17 Men’s World Cup in Qatar. Swami (15) and Tajikistan midfielder Komiljon Zoirshohovich Sharipov (15) have become the first players to compete at both levels of FIFA’s youth World Cup competitions. Both were born in 2011 and represented their countries at the U-15 tournament in Baku in late October.

news.title: Former Ferns coach Tom Sermanni helps PNG chase World Cup dream
news.lede: Former Football Ferns head coach Tom Sermanni is helping Papua New Guinea prepare for their bid to reach the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The experienced Scottish coach has joined PNG’s technical support team as they prepare for three intercontinental play-off matches in Morocco. Sermanni (72) and fellow technical expert Mark Arnot have spent recent months working with PNG’s coaching staff in Port Moresby. Main photo: Tom Sermanni … another World Cup campaign.
